title: What It Actually Takes to Build a Software Factory — Tereza Tížková, Factory
talk_summary: Tereza Tížková describes Factory's production 'software factory': an orchestrator/worker/validator agent loop with a pre-written validation contract, model routing by task-difficulty classification, deferred tool context, and codebase 'agent readiness' hygiene. The concrete, copyable mechanisms are sequential worker chains with independent validators, user-testing validators in real VMs, and progressive tool disclosure.

takeaways.technique: Validation contract written before code + independent validators
takeaways.what_they_do: The orchestrator writes a 'validation contract' defining done before any code exists; validators judge code they did not write, split into a scrutiny validator (liners/types/tests) and a user-testing validator that actually clicks through the product in a VM.

takeaways.technique: Sequential worker chain, not a swarm
takeaways.what_they_do: Workers run in sequence passing output to the next, each with fresh context, while each worker may fan out parallel sub-agents for small tasks (web research, file building).
takeaways.evidence_quote: they work in a sequence. So they don't work in a swarm or parallel ... you end up with more fresh context

takeaways.what_they_do: Classify task difficulty from prompt/codebase/tools, set a capability threshold, pick the cheapest model predicted to clear it, and escalate mid-task only on failure; also set per-role default models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you choose the cheapest model above the threshold ... cheapest model that is predicted to accomplish your task

takeaways.what_they_do: Nothing is removed, just hidden until needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we just progressively disclose what's in the context and what tools to use ... nothing is actually removed it's just hidden
takeaways.numbers: claims 50%+ token savings at scale with many tools

takeaways.what_they_do: Package reusable skills, context and conventions as plugins that auto-update docs; run an 'agent readiness' checklist (reproducible dev env, tests, docs, lint/style) before scaling agent adoption.
takeaways.evidence_quote: plugins which are like packaged reusable skills and context ... automatically updating our documentations

takeaways.what_they_do: Treats defining 'done' as the hard part of loops; warns agents will game tests that are written wrong, so criteria must be verifiable and not just test-passing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you write the what it means to be done in the wrong way, the agent can try to pass your tests but not really
